items.q: Keeping the ties of kinship.
Being good and dutiful to parents.
The word "rahim" (womb, kinship) comes from the same root as this Name of Allah.

Marriage in Arabic.
The gift the husband must give the wife at marriage.
The wedding feast.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ said "the best of you are the best to" these (paraphrased).
The verse "And We have enjoined on man goodness to his parents" (meaning); his mother carried him in this state.
Saying "uff" to parents is forbidden in this surah.
The du'a for parents, "My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small" (meaning), is in this surah.

The verse that lists the women one may not marry.

Giving a newborn's name on the seventh day with a sacrifice.

Spending on poor relatives earns this double reward.

The period a woman waits after divorce or her husband's death.

The 'iddah of a pregnant woman.
The surah named after divorce.

The women forbidden by blood include the mother, daughter, sister, aunts and these.
The women forbidden by marriage ties include the wife's mother and this.

items.q: Our Beloved Master ﷺ said a woman is married for four things: wealth, lineage, beauty and this.
Seeing the person one plans to marry is allowed, said our Beloved Prophet ﷺ to this Companion.
A man may have up to this many wives, with justice.
The verse says if you fear you cannot be just, then marry this many.
Divorce that can be taken back within the 'iddah.
The number of divorces after which remarriage is not allowed until she marries another.
A woman seeking separation by giving back the mahr.
Custody of young children after divorce.

In the Hanafi school, the mother has custody of a girl until about this age.
In the Shafi'i school, a child of discernment chooses between parents at about this age.
After the mother, the next in line for custody in the Hanafi school.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ judged that a maternal aunt is like this, in custody.
The daughter of our master Hamzah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) was given to the care of this aunt.
Maintenance (nafaqah) for poor parents is owed by this person.
In the Hanafi school, maintenance is owed to every poor mahram relative by this measure.
In the Shafi'i school, maintenance is owed only to these relatives.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ told Hind (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا) she may take from her husband's wealth this much.

Swearing not to approach one's wife for four months or more.

items.q: Asked which deed Allah loves most, our Beloved Master ﷺ said prayer on time, then this (paraphrased).

The wife of Thabit ibn Qays (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا) who asked for khul' and returned his garden.
